NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493,
  2498, 2499, 2503, 2505, 2507, and proposed Resolution No. 2512, due to the continuing state of
  emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19
  virus, this meeting is being broadcast via teleconference. Members of the public may participate in-person
  in the Council Chambers, or virtually in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 879 7827 2172, Meeting Password: 339794. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call in ption from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 879 7827 2172 , Meeting Password: 339794. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  FY 2022-23 BUDGET PUBLIC HEARING AND ADOPTION

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) open the Public Hearing and take any public
  testimony related to the budget adoption including appropriation limit, fees & charges, fund
  balance policy and investment policy; 2) close the Public Hearing; and 3) review and adopt
  Resolutions 2509, 2510, and 2511, Statement of Fund Balance Policy, and Statement of
  Investment Policy.

Director Whitehead introduced Accountant Estrada who provided a summary of the staff report (as
per the staff report).

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, MAYOR ZERUNYAN so moved.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA stated that regarding horse trainer fees, she had previously
suggested broadening the definition of “horse trainers” and changing it to “horse professionals”
when it relates to trail rides for the purpose of including all types of horse trainers including those
who operate trail rides.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JUNE 28, 2022
 COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA inquired about an email that was received from a horse trainer –
who has an assistant. Per the City’s policy, as she reads it, the assistant would also be classified
as a horse trainer - category 3. She asked for clarification.

Attorney Davis stated that staff has been working on a draft ordinance to amend and restate the
Horse Trainer Permit Chapter 5.40 to include the proposed term, “Horse Trail Operators.”

Assistant City Manager Davis stated that regarding the Horse Trainer License, the intent is to
broaden the “horse trainer” term categories to include the use of facilities including City trails and
arenas. The fees and proposed ordinance have been reviewed by the Parks & Activities
Commission and the Equestrian Committee.

Assistant City Manager Davis stated that regarding the public comment, if the subcontractor
currently receives a business license, they will continue to receive a business license and permit;
the requirement for a business license is dependent on how the business is formed.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, MAYOR ZERUNYAN so moved.
